(Atlanta, Georgia) | college = [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]] (2019–2020) | highlights = * Second-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] (2020) * [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|SEC Freshman of the Year]] (2020) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2019 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2019]]) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2019) * [[Ballislife All-American Game|Ballislife All-American]] (2019) | medal_templates = }} '''Anthony Edwards''' (born August 5, 2001) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia Bulldogs]]. Listed at {{convert|6|ft|4|in|m|2}} and {{convert|225|lbs|kg|0}}, he plays the [[shooting guard]] position. Edwards finished his high school career at [[Holy Spirit Preparatory School]] in his hometown of [[Atlanta]], where he was rated a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the best players in the 2019 class by major recruiting services. As a senior, he earned [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] and [[USA Today All-USA high school basketball team|''USA Today'' All-USA first team]] honors. He committed to play college basketball for Georgia, becoming the most heralded recruit to do so, and was named [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|SEC Freshman of the Year]] after his freshman season with the team. ==Early life== Edwards was brought up in [[Atlanta|Atlanta, Georgia]]. When he was three years old, he was given the nickname "Ant-Man" by his father. For much of his childhood, Edwards played [[American football|football]] at the [[running back]], [[quarterback]], and [[cornerback]] positions.{{cite web |last1=O'Donnell |first1=Ricky |title=The origin story of high school basketball’s ‘Ant-Man’ |url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2019/1/15/18139281/anthony-edwards-basketball-recruiting-nba-draft |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |accessdate=April 25, 2019 |date=January 15, 2019}} He played youth football for the Atlanta Vikings and became one of the best [[Pop Warner Little Scholars|Pop Warner]] running backs in the country by age 10.{{cite web |last1=Jones |first1=Ryan |title=Anthony Edwards Is Ready For the Next Level |url=https://www.slamonline.com/the-magazine/anthony-edwards-story/ |publisher=[[Slam (magazine)|Slam]] |accessdate=April 25, 2019 |date=April 12, 2019}}{{cite web |last1=Westerholm |first1=Tom |title=Anthony Edwards, No. 4 prospect in 2019, honed toughness, intangibles as a football player |url=https://www.masslive.com/hoophallclassic/2019/01/anthony_edwards_no_4_prospect_1.html |website=[[The Republican (Springfield, Massachusetts)|The Republican]] |accessdate=April 25, 2019 |date=January 21, 2019}} However, Edwards switched his focus to basketball because he "thought it looked more fun" after watching his brothers play the sport. He often played basketball against his brothers at their grandmother's house. Entering ninth grade, he began training under the guidance of Justin Holland, a former [[college basketball]] player for [[Liberty Flames basketball|Liberty]] and an Atlanta-based basketball trainer. ==High school career== Due to his success with the Atlanta Xpress 15-under [[Amateur Athletic Union]] team, Edwards was considered a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] in 2016.{{cite web |last1=McDonald |first1=Dan |title=Four-star SG Anthony Edwards making moves |url=https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/four-star-sg-anthony-edwards-making-moves |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |accessdate=April 26, 2019 |date=March 12, 2017}} He began playing high school basketball for [[Therrell High School]] in Atlanta as a member of the 2019 class.{{cite web |last1=Krohn |first1=Adam |title=Life ordinary for nation’s top basketball prospect Edwards |url=https://www.ajc.com/blog/high-school-sports/life-ordinary-for-nation-top-prospect-edwards/lEvjBtck7UXhdmNko50nDL/ |website=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] |accessdate=April 26, 2019 |date=January 15, 2019}} In early January 2017, Edwards transferred to [[Holy Spirit Preparatory School]] in Atlanta and reclassified to the 2020 class. He made the move in an effort to improve his academic performance, since Holy Spirit Preparatory had "small class sizes and support to help that."{{cite web |last1=Neysmith |first1=Horace |title=Anthony Edwards is a name to remember |url=https://www.allmetrohoops.com/news_article/show/773519 |publisher=AllMetroHoops |accessdate=April 26, 2019 |date=March 24, 2017}} In March 2018, Edwards helped Holy Spirit Preparatory defeat [[The Heritage School (Newnan, Georgia)|The Heritage School]] for the [[Georgia Independent School Association]] (GISA) Class AAA state championship.{{cite web |title=Holy Spirit Preparatory boys successfully defend state basketball title |url=https://georgiabulletin.org/news/2018/03/holy-spirit-preparatory-boys-successfully-defend-state-basketball-title/ |website=The Georgia Bulletin |accessdate=April 26, 2019 |date=March 22, 2018}} He reclassified back to the 2019 class in November 2018 after seeing academic improvement.{{cite web |last1=Nutter |first1=Gage |title=Anthony Edwards' reclassification decision came down to family |url=https://www.masslive.com/hoophallclassic/2019/01/anthony_edwards_reclassificati.html |website=[[The Republican (Springfield, Massachusetts)|The Republican]] |accessdate=April 27, 2019 |date=January 21, 2019}} As a result, Edwards rose to become the number one recruit in the Top247 rankings by recruiting website [[247Sports.com|247Sports]].{{cite web |last1=Daniels |first1=Evan |title=Anthony Edwards reclassifies, is new No. 1 player in Top247 |url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Anthony-Edwards-reclassifies-is-new-No-1-player-in-Top247-125027525/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |accessdate=April 27, 2019 |date=November 20, 2018}} In his senior season, his team finished as GISA Class AAA runners-up to The Heritage School, despite 27 [[Point (basketball)|points]] from Edwards.{{cite web |last1=Gorman |first1=Doug |title=Heritage dethrones Holy Spirit |url=http://times-herald.com/news/2019/02/heritage-dethrones-holy-spirit |website=[[Newnan Times-Herald]] |accessdate=April 27, 2019 |date=February 26, 2019}} At the end of the season, he was averaging 29 points, nine [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], and two [[Assist (basketball)|assists]] per game.{{cite web |last1=Divens |first1=Jordan |title=MaxPreps 2018–19 High School Boys Basketball All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/mdbwDYCSa02E7-TpRc5Gmg/maxpreps-2018-19-high-school-boys-basketball-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |accessdate=April 27, 2019 |date=April 11, 2019}} Edwards garnered [[USA Today All-USA high school basketball team|''USA Today'' All-USA first team]] and [[MaxPreps]] All-American fourth team recognition.{{cite web |title=2018–19 ALL-USA High School Boys Basketball: First Team |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2019/2018-19-all-usa-high-school-boys-basketball-first-team |publisher=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=April 27, 2019 |date=April 2, 2019}} He played in the [[2019 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]] and [[Jordan Brand Classic]] in March and April 2019, respectively.{{cite web |title=Holy Spirit's Edwards gets McDonald's All-American Games jersey |url=https://www.mdjonline.com/neighbor_newspapers/northside_sandy_springs/sports/holy-spirit-s-edwards-gets-mcdonald-s-all-american-games/article_59379b24-4db3-11e9-bab4-270ca73c2e03.html |website=[[Marietta Daily Journal]] |accessdate=April 27, 2019 |date=March 23, 2019}}{{cite web |last1=Armstrong |first1=Megan |title=Cole Anthony, James Wiseman Win Co-MVP; White Wins 2019 Jordan Brand Classic |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2832315-cole-anthony-james-wiseman-win-co-mvp-white-wins-2019-jordan-brand-classic |publisher=[[Bleacher Report]] |accessdate=April 27, 2019 |date=April 20, 2019}} ===Recruiting=== By consensus among major recruiting services [[247Sports.com|247Sports]], [[ESPN]], and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], Edwards was rated a five-star recruit, top-five player, and the top [[shooting guard]] in the 2019 class.{{cite web |title=Anthony Edwards, 2019 Shooting guard |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2019/anthony-edwards-181409 |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |accessdate=April 27, 2019}}{{cite web |title=Anthony Edwards, Holy Spirit Preparatory School, Shooting Guard |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Anthony-Edwards-45572558/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |accessdate=April 27, 2019}}{{cite web |title=Anthony Edwards |url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/228812/anthony-edwards |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=April 27, 2019}} On February 11, 2019, he committed to play college basketball for [[Georgia Bulldogs men's basketball|Georgia]], becoming the program's best recruit in the modern recruiting era.{{cite web |last1=Adams |first1=Kipp |title=Where Anthony Edwards ranks among Georgia’s all-time recruits |url=https://247sports.com/college/georgia/Article/Georgia-Basketball-Recruiting-Anthony-Edwards-recruiting-rankings-National-Signing-Day-2019-129028577/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |accessdate=April 27, 2019 |date=February 12, 2019}}{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Guard Anthony Edwards opts to stay at home, commits to Georgia |url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/25971814/guard-anthony-edwards-opts-stay-home-commits-georgia |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=April 27, 2019 |date=February 11, 2019}} Edwards chose the Bulldogs over offers from [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], and [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]]. Edwards was drawn to Georgia because two of his favorite players, [[Dwyane Wade]] and [[Victor Oladipo]], had been coached in college by head coach [[Tom Crean (basketball)|Tom Crean]].{{cite web |last1=Polacek |first1=Scott |title=5-Star SG Anthony Edwards Commits to Georgia; Potential No. 1 for 2020 NBA Draft |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2808426-5-star-sg-anthony-edwards-commits-to-georgia-potential-no-1-for-2020-nba-draft |publisher=[[Bleacher Report]] |accessdate=November 26, 2019 |date=February 11, 2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Anthony Edwards | position = [[Shooting guard|SG]] | hometown = [[Atlanta|Atlanta, GA]] | highschool = [[Holy Spirit Preparatory School|Holy Spirit Prep]] (GA) | feet = 6 | inches = 4 | weight = 205 | 40 = | commitdate = February 11, 2019 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 96 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2019 | rivals ref title = Georgia 2019 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2019 Georgia Bulldogs Recruiting Class | rivals school = georgia | scout s = | espn schoolid = 61 | 247 overall = 1 | rivals overall = 3 | espn overall = 4 | accessdate = January 29, 2019 | bball = yes }} ==College career== [[File:Anthony Edwards Georgia 2 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Edwards in February 2020]] On November 5, 2019, Edwards made his debut for Georgia, recording 24 points, nine rebounds, and four [[Steal (basketball)|steals]] in a 91–72 win over [[Western Carolina Catamounts men's basketball|Western Carolina]]. It was the most points by a Georgia freshman debutant since [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame|Basketball Hall of Fame]] inductee [[Dominique Wilkins]] in 1979.{{cite news |title=Edwards debuts with 24 points as Georgia beats Catamounts |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169800 |accessdate=November 6, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 5, 2019}} On November 26, he scored a season-high 37 points, including 33 in the second half, and posted six rebounds, four steals, and three [[Block (basketball)|blocks]] in a 93–85 loss to third-ranked [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]] at the [[2019 Maui Invitational Tournament|Maui Invitational]]. Edwards became the first Georgia freshman to score at least 37 points in a game since [[Jacky Dorsey]] in 1975.{{cite web |title=Georgia’s Comeback Effort Falls Short in 93–85 Loss to No. 3 Michigan State |url=https://georgiadogs.com/news/2019/11/26/mens-basketball-georgias-comeback-effort-falls-short-in-93-85-loss-to-no-3-michigan-state.aspx |publisher=University of Georgia Athletics |accessdate=November 26, 2019 |date=November 26, 2019}} In his final game at the tournament, he led all scorers with 24 points and made the game-winning shot against [[NCAA Division II]] team [[Chaminade Silverswords|Chaminade]].{{cite web |last1=Austin |first1=Brooks |title=Anthony Edwards Hits Game Winning Shot for the Georgia Bulldogs |url=https://www.si.com/college/georgia/news/anthony-edwards-hits-game-winning-shot |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |accessdate=January 6, 2020 |date=November 27, 2019}} On February 1, 2020, Edwards recorded 29 points and 15 rebounds, both game-highs, in a 63–48 victory over [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]].{{cite web |title=Edwards Second-Straight Double-Double Powers Georgia over Texas A&M, 63–48 |url=https://georgiadogs.com/news/2020/2/1/mens-basketball-edwards-second-straight-double-double-powers-georgia-over-texas-am-63-48.aspx |publisher=University of Georgia Athletics |accessdate=February 6, 2020 |date=February 1, 2020}} In his next game, he led all scorers with 32 points in an 81–75 loss to [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]].{{cite web |title=Georgia Falls at Florida, 81–75 |url=https://georgiadogs.com/news/2020/2/5/mens-basketball-georgia-falls-flat-at-florida-81-75.aspx |publisher=University of Georgia Athletics |accessdate=February 6, 2020 |date=February 5, 2020}} On February 26, Edwards scored 36 points and collected seven rebounds, four assists and four steals, in a 94–90 [[Overtime (sports)|overtime]] defeat to [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]].{{cite web |last1=Griffith |first1=Mike |title=Edwards scores 36 but Bulldogs lose in OT |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/edwards-scores-but-bulldogs-lose/nblmmS9AN2X8xR1Xp50FpM/ |website=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] |accessdate=March 11, 2020 |date=February 26, 2020}} As a freshman, he averaged 19.1 points, 5.2 rebounds and 2.8 assists per game.{{cite web |last1=Dortch |first1=Chris |title=Georgia's Anthony Edwards armed with NBA athleticism, NBA strength |url=https://www.nba.com/article/2020/03/20/georgia-anthony-edwards-draft-feature |publisher=[[National Basketball Association|NBA]] |accessdate=March 24, 2020 |date=March 20, 2020}} Edwards was the top scorer on his team and among freshmen nationally. He earned second-team All-SEC and [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|SEC Freshman of the Year]] honors.{{cite press release|url=https://www.secsports.com/article/28877731/sec-announces-2020-men-basketball-awards |title=SEC announces 2020 Men's Basketball Awards |publisher=Southeastern Conference |date=March 10, 2020 |accessdate=March 10, 2020}} Edwards collected SEC Freshman of the Week accolades four times during the season, the most in program history.{{cite web |last1=Jackson |first1=Jordan |title=Anthony Edwards Named SEC Freshman of the Year |url=https://www.si.com/college/georgia/news/anthony-edwards-named-sec-freshman-of-the-year |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |accessdate=March 24, 2020 |date=March 10, 2020}} He was also one of five finalists for the [[Jerry West Award]], which recognizes the top collegiate [[shooting guard]].{{cite web |title=Georgia’s Edwards finalist for Jerry West Shooting Guard award |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/college/georgia-edwards-finalist-for-jerry-west-shooting-guard-award/fJITgXuu9YwXUBcNuF20AM/ |website=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] |accessdate=March 24, 2020 |date=March 3, 2020}} On March 20, 2020, Edwards declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]] as one of the most touted prospects in his class. He signed with an [[sports agent|agent]], forgoing his remaining college basketball eligibility.{{cite web |title=No. 1 prospect Anthony Edwards of Georgia declares for NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28931229/no-1-prospect-anthony-edwards-georgia-declares-nba-draft |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=March 24, 2020 |date=March 20, 2020}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20]]{{cite web |title=Anthony Edwards College Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/anthony-edwards-2.html |publisher=[[Sports Reference]] |accessdate=March 24, 2020}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 Georgia Bulldogs basketball team|Georgia]] | 32 || 32 || 33.0 || .402 || .294 || .772 || 5.2 || 2.8 || 1.3 || .6 || 19.1 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Edwards' mother, Yvette, and grandmother, Shirley, both died from cancer during an eight-month span in 2015, when he was in eighth grade. He has worn the {{abbr|No.|Number}} 5 basketball jersey since high school to honor them, as they both died on the fifth day of the month.{{cite web |last1=Daniels |first1=Evan |title=Self-made man: How Anthony Edwards became an elite NBA prospect |url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Self-made-man-How-Anthony-Edwards-became-an-elite-NBA-prospect-141553138/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |accessdate=January 6, 2020 |date=January 3, 2020}} In turn, Edwards was raised by his sister, Antoinette, and brother, Antoine, who share [[child custody|legal custody]] over him.{{cite web |last1=Towers |first1=Chip |title=Top-ranked prospect Anthony ‘Ant Man’ Edwards has made his college decision |url=https://www.dawgnation.com/mens-basketball/anthony-edwards-georgia-basketball-2019 |publisher=DawgNation |accessdate=April 26, 2019}} In high school, Edwards frequently worked as an instructor at a number of youth camps.{{cite web |last1=Pourtout |first1=E. Marcel |title=Bulldog-bound Edwards leading Cougars on another title run |url=https://www.mdjonline.com/neighbor_newspapers/northside_sandy_springs/sports/bulldog-bound-edwards-leading-cougars-on-another-title-run/article_2413a1a2-35d2-11e9-8d79-77893d912431.html |website=[[Marietta Daily Journal]] |accessdate=April 27, 2019 |date=February 21, 2019}} He intended to major in [[marketing]] while attending the [[University of Georgia]].{{cite web |title=Anthony Edwards – 2019–20 – Men's Basketball |url=https://georgiadogs.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4098 |publisher=University of Georgia Athletics |accessdate=November 6, 2019}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://georgiadogs.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/anthony-edwards/4098 Georgia Bulldogs bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Edwards, Anthony}} [[Category:2001 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Georgia (U.S. state)]] [[Category:Georgia Bulldogs basketball players]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Atlanta]]
